key_insight: Simulation-only reinforcement learning enabled an open-weight 27B reasoning model to control real robots without demonstrations, achieving 60% success in reported real-world trials.
engineering_relevance: The approach suggests a path to robot control through foundation-model post-training, with transfer to unseen hardware and novel instructions.
method: Build PEAR, a post-training engine for scalable simulated robot tasks.
Apply robot-use reinforcement learning on LIBERO and RoboDojo without demonstrations.
Train the model to observe, reason, and directly generate end-effector poses.
evidence_signal: Reported success rose from 1.6% to 74.4% on LIBERO and from 0% to 60% on a real dual-arm robot; on LIBERO-Pro task changes, the model achieved 57.4% versus 0.75% for π₀.₅.
watch_item: The abstract does not report real-world trial counts or safety evaluations, limiting confidence in deployment reliability.
paper_title: Training Reasoning Models in Simulation to Natively Use Real Robots
